The Chuquisaca Revolution was a rising in the city of Chuquisaca, now Sucre, on 25 May 1809, in which judges, lawyers and students of its university removed the Spanish governor. It is often called the first cry of independence in Spanish America.

Chuquisaca was the seat of the Audiencia of Charcas, the royal court that governed what is now Bolivia, and of a famous university that trained many leaders of independence. When Spain fell to Napoleon, rival groups argued over who should rule. The rising was followed in July by another in La Paz.

Both were crushed by troops from Peru and Buenos Aires, and the leaders in La Paz were hanged. War dragged on for sixteen years in the highlands, until Sucre's army won. The city now bears his name. Bolivia's struggle was part of the Spanish American wars of independence.
